source.title: Towards explaining the generalization gap in neural networks using topological data analysis
source.authors: Rubén Ballester; Xavier Arnal Clemente; C. Casacuberta; M. Madadi; C. Corneanu; Sergio Escalera

record.file_problem: The supplied text contains the full paper and appendix. The title in the supplied metadata differs slightly from the title in the paper text.
record.tranche_reason: The study tests whether a different measured property—topological summaries of neuron activation correlations—tracks the generalization gap, using cross-validated prediction.
record.gate_note: The study reports cross-validated R² scores for topological-summary predictors and describes architecture clusters associated with the gap. It does not test the specific claim versions about memorization, width, architectures, optimizers, batch size, dropout, magnitude-aware sharpness, or removing memorized examples.
record.test_reason: The study evaluates activation-correlation topology as a predictor of generalization gaps, not any of V1–V8. In particular, it neither measures magnitude-aware weight-perturbation sharpness nor compares that measure with norms or margins, so its results do not test V7. Its architecture clusters concern depth within convolutional families, not convolutional versus fully connected networks as in V3.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate. The authors report competitive gap prediction using functional-graph persistence summaries, with average location and dispersion performing best. Their method ranks second by mean R² on both tasks; they also report depth-dependent clustering and call for broader validation across architectures and tasks.
record.recipe_differences: Uses activation-correlation functional graphs and persistence-diagram summaries to predict gaps across trained networks; it does not apply the claim versions' interventions or measures.
record.method_sensitivity: Prediction scores differ by task and homological dimension; the authors report stronger and more conclusive results for Task 2 than Task 1, and generally better scores in dimension 1. Adding squared summaries raises R² scores.

fits_no_version.finding: Topological-summary regressions predict generalization gaps with best cross-validated R² of 0.5601 ± 0.13 on CIFAR10 and 0.9337 ± 0.01 on SVHN. Average and standard deviation of persistence births and deaths yield the strongest summaries.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Summaries of persistence diagrams derived from neuron activation correlations can predict generalization gaps across trained image classifiers, with performance depending on task and summary choice.

record.problems: The authors note that sampling may lose information and that broader experiments across other network types and tasks are needed. The analysis uses only two PGDL tasks and sampled neurons and inputs.
record.rows_left_out: No separate rows for other tested persistence-summary combinations or state-of-the-art comparison methods; Table 1 reports only the top three combinations per task, and the other combinations are displayed in Figure 4.2. The state-of-the-art comparison rows concern comparator predictors rather than the study's topological properties.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting and the corresponding natural-label and random-label held-out accuracies.
Test error as width increases beyond the width required for zero training error.
Convolutional versus fully connected generalization, local connectivity, sparse connections, and transferred initialization.
Adaptive versus SGD held-out performance under different tuning and optimizer recipes.
Batch-size effects under fixed epoch budgets and recipe adaptations.
Dropout effects, small-data and underfitting regimes, and joint removal of dropout and weight decay.
Magnitude-aware sharpness versus generalization gaps and its ranking relative to norm- and margin-based measures.
Retraining after removing highly memorized examples versus equally many random examples.

record.verdict_notes: The six numerical values and conditions agree with Table 1; their uncertainties are standard deviations across ten cross-validation scores. Observed predictive performance cannot establish any listed version. Citations to original sources supply background rather than tests.

versions.untested_parts: Memorization of random labels and generalization on natural labels.
Width sweep beyond the interpolation threshold.
Convolutional versus fully connected architecture comparisons.
Adaptive versus SGD optimizer comparisons and tuning or recipe changes.
Batch-size comparisons and changes to the training recipe.
Magnitude-aware weight perturbation sharpness and comparisons with norm- or margin-based measures.

rows.subject: 96 VGG-like neural networks
rows.operation_detail: Predict generalization gap from average and standard deviation of births and deaths, plus their squared values, using linear regression.
rows.measure: Mean R² test score for generalization-gap prediction
rows.note: Aggregate across the task's network set and the 10 experiments of the 5 × 2-fold cross-validation statistical test.
rows.check: The value matches Table 1, but it measures the study's gap-prediction method's performance, not a listed claim's effect. Retain only as a fits_no_version finding.
